items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Knowledge and experience in analyzing complex situations and identifying solutions for problem-solving; skills and experience in developing and administering programs designed to meet the diverse needs of students.
Knowledge and experience in researching, compiling and analyzing data, and generating reports.
Knowledge of and experience in conflict management and intervention strategies.
Program Implementation and Student Support — 50%
Under guidance from the Assistant Dean, implement and administer MPS student success programs, including MPS Scholars and the NSF S-STEM Scholarship Program.

Coordinate MPS Scholars and NSF S-STEM programs, providing holistic academic, financial, and developmental support to mathematical and physical sciences students, with a special emphasis on supporting low-income, first-generation, transfer, and underrepresented students.

Implement outreach strategies to reach eligible students; develop and implement program-specific application and selection processes; and coordinate student selection, welcome messaging, and orientation activities.

Manage support for participating students, including housing, meals, field trips, group study sessions, community-building activities, and other enrichment programs; monitor and support student progress.

Assist in the development and implementation of programming designed to enhance undergraduate and graduate student success, including recruitment and orientation activities, mentoring initiatives, professional development programming, research preparation pathways, graduate school preparation, and community building.
Support students in addressing academic, financial, personal, and identity-related challenges that may affect their ability to remain enrolled and complete their degrees.

Assist in the development of curriculum for innovative academic and professional development seminars/courses and other programs, activities, and events that support student achievement, professional development, and workforce placement.

Coordinate the MPS Scholars mentoring network, including recruitment, pairing, orientation, and training of mentors and mentees; design and coordinate related events and professional development opportunities.
Coordinate retreats, conferences, orientations, workshops, forums, and other activities in consultation with program leadership and in coordination with appropriate campus partners.
Coordinate MPS 101 course activities, including guest speakers, course materials, and support for faculty instructors, GSIs, and students.
Develop and distribute program communications and documents, including website updates, marketing materials, forms, policy statements, and other program materials.

Work collaboratively with staff, faculty, administrators, alumni, students, departments, and partner institutions to generate innovative approaches to meeting the needs of undergraduate and graduate students and postdoctoral fellows.
Represent MPS programs to various constituencies and on campus committees and cross-departmental collaborations.
Coordinate with participating colleges, departments, advisers, and partner institutions to resolve academic and career counseling concerns and advocate for MPS Scholars students.
Develop strategic partnerships with faculty, administrators, alumni, and external stakeholders to expand research, funding, internship, career, and professional opportunities for students.
Lead the work of graduate and peer mentors, student staff, and professional staff supporting MPS Scholars, NSF S-STEM, and other programs in the MPS assistant dean's office.
Recruit, assist with, and support the training and orientation of mentors, peer staff, tutors, and other student program personnel.
Provide ongoing direction and support to assigned student and program staff to ensure effective delivery of program activities and services.
Program Resource and Funding Coordination - 15%

Collaborates with program leadership and finance offices to monitor program resources and ensure program activities and expenditures align with applicable grant requirements, funding restrictions, and program objectives.
Contributes to external grant development, including drafts of program design narratives, evidence-based intervention strategies, and alignment of proposed initiatives with funding priorities.
Works with guidance from program leaders to identify and pursue funding opportunities and revenue streams and supports engagement with alumni and donors.
Program Assessment, Evaluation and Reporting — 10%

In coordination with the Assistant Dean and Research Associate, implement program evaluation frameworks and assessment instruments; collect quantitative and qualitative data and generate reports for federal sponsors, institutional leadership, and external stakeholders.
Work with the Research Associate and program leadership to monitor program implementation, participation, outcomes, and overall program success.
Analyze program information and recommend changes to program content, processes, and procedures to improve program effectiveness and student outcomes.

Coordinate interim and annual program reporting, gather and compile data, draft narrative content, and contribute to reports and scholarly publications related to student success and program outcomes.
Assist program leadership in establishing and implementing program objectives and short- and long-term strategies.
Professional, Collaborative and Special Projects — 5%
Maintain professional knowledge related to student success, academic support, mentoring, and program administration and participate in relevant professional development activities.
Provide guidance and program-related information to faculty, staff, administrators, students, alumni, and other stakeholders.
Facilitate collaboration among participating departments, colleges, campus units, and external partners.
Support special projects and other MPS Dean's Office initiatives as assigned.
Travel as needed, including occasional overnight and weekend travel.
Demonstrated knowledge of the theories and practice of learning, counseling, human and career development.

Knowledge in how to enhance students' intellectual and personal growth and development, including critical thinking, effective communication, self-appraisal, self-esteem, clarification of values, appropriate career choices, and leadership.

Knowledge of the methodologies used to enhance student achievement, such as collaborative teaching / learning models, strategies for effective advising, counseling, faculty, near-peer, and peer mentoring, small group facilitation and training, coaching, mentoring, and advocacy.
Knowledge of trends and issues facing low-income and first-generation college, underrepresented, disadvantaged, physically challenged, and under prepared students in higher education.
Knowledge of research methodologies and research designs.
Knowledge of federal, state, and local requirements to provide for access, health, confidentiality, and safety; legal and ethical issues governing the delivery of counseling services.
